# Remapper

## Save IDs to run in remapper
```{r Remapper}

```

## Run remapper

* Restricts to only participants for who we have genotype data for
* And adds FID and IID and genetic sex

```{}
/path_three/Release11_Observed/GWAS_ID_remapper -headerline -intabdelim -dropancestryoutliers -removeduplicates -numericids=MDD -useQSKIN=NO -subset=Full_Observed -repeatoriginalid -outpedigree /path_one/AGDS/Natural_disasters_AGDS/R/data/AGDS_all4surveys_phenotype_IDs.txt > /path_one/AGDS/Natural_disasters_AGDS/R/data/AGDS_all4surveys_phenotype_IDs_remapper.txt
```



## Add 10 PCs

* PCs have already been made for all QIMR genotype data.
* Add 10 PCs and add as columns to file - to be used to account for ancestry differences.
* Match on column 2 (IID) in our remapper file and extracting columns 6-15 (PC1-10) from the principal component scores file, then printing these at the end of our remapper file = from column 11 as we have 10 columns already.

```{}
awk 'NR==FNR{A[$2]=$6 FS $7 FS $8 FS $9 FS $10 FS $11 FS $12 FS $13 FS $14 FS $15; next}(FNR==1){print $0, "PC1","PC2","PC3","PC4","PC5","PC6","PC7","PC8","PC9","PC10"; next} {$11=A[$2]}1' /path_three/Release11_Observed/AncestryChecks/GWAS_PrincipalComponentsScores.txt /path_one/AGDS/Natural_disasters_AGDS/R/data/AGDS_all4surveys_phenotype_IDs_remapper.txt > /path_one/AGDS/Natural_disasters_AGDS/R/data/AGDS_all4surveys_phenotype_IDs_remapper_PCs.txt
```

# Relatedness

* Input list of FID IID to plink to calculate relatedness of individuals

## Save list of IDs

* Save list of AGDS IDs with which to calculate relatedness

```{}
awk '{print $1,$2}' /path_one/AGDS/Natural_disasters_AGDS/R/data/AGDS_all4surveys_phenotype_IDs_remapper.txt > AGDS_IDs.txt
```

## Calculate pihat in PLINK

* Used script /path_one/Reference/Relatedness/01_AGDS_relatedness.sh

```{}
module load plink/1.90b7.4
plink --bfile /path_three/Release11_Observed/PLINK_format/GWAS_Build37PlusStrand \
 --chr 1-22 \
 --extract /path_one/Reference/GWAS_reference/R11_observed_genotypes_GSAchip_autosomes/Observed_genotypes_GSAchip_autosomes_MAF0.01_Geno0.02_Mind0.02_HWE0.0000000001_LD0.2.prune.in \
 --keep /path_one/AGDS/Natural_disasters_AGDS/R/data/AGDS_IDs.txt \
 --genome \
 --out AGDS_relatedness \
 --threads 2 \
 --min 0.1

```

# Outcome Variable: No. Symptoms

* Count data so could try poisson or negative binomial
  + But bounded, top no. = 9 and very heavily skewed for some
* May be better to do a binomial distribution with Bernoulli trials
  + Each symptom is a ‘trial’ with a yes or no, total no. trials/symptoms = 9
  + But assumes a collection of independent and identically distributed (the success probability p is constant and the same for all the N trials.)     
  + Depressive symptoms can't really be considered independent
* Ordinal regression
  + Allows non-independent events (this method is superior for handling the case when the Bernoulli outcomes contributing the binomial event are possibly non-independent and possible non-identical in their probability)
  + Proportional odds model / ordinal logit model
  + Proportional odds model fits a series of logistic regressions for each level (i.e. for each no. symptoms, generates multiple stratified binomial models
  + But different interpretation (can just say higher odds of having more symptoms, not an amount increase in symptoms 
* If we look at the distributions for each below we can see that for natural disaster (worst depression) and natural disaster (first depression) there are some instances where 1, 2 or 3 symptoms only occurs for people experiencing no ND (this no. of symptoms not present in anyone who does experience a ND)
* Therefore if run an ordinal regression with 9 categories this runs into problems of singularity
* Group symptoms into 0 = 0, 1 - 3 = low, 4 - 6 = medium, 7 - 9 = high
  + Could group 0 symptoms with 1 - 3 in low. But it may be that a different process is involved in have no versus even 1 symptom, they seem more different than 1 -> 2 -> 3 symptoms so keep as their own category.

```{r CodeNUMSYMPALLCategories}

```

* So best to use PO model
